Subject: Pilot credits & commit-tier packaging for Acme Health pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the latency profile and KV-cache primitives look promising for our triage assistant POC. Procurement asked me to confirm two things before we lock the pilot:

1) Pilot credits: how many free tokens/credits do you typically provide for a 30-day POC? Our initial plan estimates ~150k tokens/day peak for ingestion & interactive testing, so something in the low millions would be ideal to avoid throttling during evaluation.

2) Commit tiers and discounts: if we convert the pilot into a committed monthly plan, what do your per-token discounts look like at different commit levels? We need to build this into our internal TCO model and present it to finance. Specifically: small pilot -> 1–3M tokens/month, mid -> 5–10M, enterprise -> 20M+. Any guidance on launch incentives (bonus credits or upfront discounts tied to commit) would be helpful.

3) Application of credits: do promo/free credits offset the first invoice only, or can we apply them over several billing periods? Also, are there any restrictions on credits (model family restrictions, embeddings vs generation)?

If you can send a short mutual action plan (timeline, deliverables, PO/procurement contacts) and a sample SOW or pilot worksheet we can share with our legal/procurement, that would accelerate the internal review.

Thanks — cc'ing Lina from product who is coordinating the technical side.

—Tom
Tom Gardner
Head of Integrations, Acme Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Pilot credits & commit-tier packaging for Acme Health pilot

Tom — really glad the demo was helpful. Quick answers below and I attached a short pilot metrics template + initial SOW draft for procurement/legal.

1) Pilot credits: We commonly offer a 30-day pilot with 1,000,000 free tokens as a standard package for POCs of this size. Given your estimate (150k/day peak), we can increase that to 3,000,000 tokens for the pilot so you don't run into throttling during load testing.

2) Commit tiers (hosted API, per-token):
- Bronze: 1–3M tokens/month commit — 10% per-token discount off list
- Silver: 5–10M tokens/month commit — 18%
- Gold: 20M+ tokens/month commit — 28%

These discounts are applied to generation tokens (per-token usage for completion + prompt). Embeddings are priced separately; we can provide a combined blended quote if you share anticipated embedding volumes.

3) Application of credits & launch incentives:
- Pilot credits apply to your billing chronologically and will be consumed first (they offset invoices until exhausted).
- We can offer a launch incentive: if you sign a 12-month commit at Gold tier within 45 days of pilot completion, we can add a one-time bonus credit of 500,000 tokens applied to the first invoice. For shorter commitments (3–6 months) we typically offer a smaller bonus credit (100–200k tokens).

Next steps I propose:
- I attach: "pilot_metrics_template.xlsx" and "Acme_SOW_draft_v1.pdf" (SOW is draft, includes standard pilot terms).
- Please share procurement contact and target PO timeline.
- If you want a tighter discount, I can escalate to Rishi (head of revenue ops) for approval; otherwise this is within my standard commercial parameters.

CC'ing Rishi & Steph to keep them aware — Rishi, suggest we put preliminary ceiling at 20% discount for evaluation and escalate for anything deeper.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — that framing is very helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and product: 

- Procurement asked whether the bonus launch credit is stackable with early-payment discounts or other promotional credits you may run. Also, is the bonus credit refundable if we don't meet a conversion threshold?

- Are those percent discounts negotiable for a committed 3-month ramp (we expect Month 1 low, Month 2 medium, Month 3 full) if we sign a 6-month commitment at 3M/month? They want clarity on whether a front-loaded ramp would still qualify for Silver pricing.

- Billing mechanics: what happens on overage if we spike above commit? Is overage billed at list price or at the committed tier price? We need predictable overage rules for our budget model.

Finally, what's the typical lead time to get the SOW/PO signed for a pilot like this? Our procurement lead (procurement@acmehealth.com) is on the thread. If you can propose a concrete mutual action plan (dates / approvals / deliverables) that maps to our internal calendar, that would help.

—Tom

Team — forwarding the thread with Acme. Procurement is asking for clearer mechanics on overage & whether launch credits can stack with other promos. I propose we offer the following special package to close the deal quickly (they're a reference-able health customer):

Proposal (special case, requires Rishi sign-off):
- Pilot: 30 days, 3,000,000 free tokens (as quoted).
- Conversion offer: If Acme signs a 6-month commit at 3M tokens/month within 45 days of pilot end, apply a 20% per-token discount for the first 3 months of billing.
- Launch incentive: one-time 100,000 token bonus credit applied to the first invoice upon conversion.
- Overage: billed at the committed tier price (i.e., if they commit to 3M/month, overage billed at the Silver per-token rate instead of list).
- Credits are non-refundable and will offset invoices chronologically; they cannot be cashed out.

Rationale: this is a mid-sized healthcare prospect with potential enterprise expansion; the package is time-limited and keeps our effective discount depth reasonable while giving them runway.

Rishi — can you confirm if revenue ops can approve a 20% discount for the first 3 months and the one-time 100k token launch credit? Steph — please flag any ops/legal constraints in SOW template (we may need to add a clause about non-refundable credits and conversion deadlines).

Forwarded message included below for context.

Thanks,
Hannah
